about: Every year Bapa was in the UK or Europe on each calendar day. Days with backup true (2 or more years) should always have a UK and Europe special picture ready. Photos: large and small copies, best first (rank 0 = the best darshan of its album). older_photos = folders in Bapa's Archive, not yet checked for Bapa: use only those where Bapa is clearly seen.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj blesses the home of Dutch devotee Jeanette Groenen
stories.story: 40 years ago today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced The Netherlands. He blessed the home of a devotee named Jeanette Groenen, a Dutch lady who had made a wish during the bicentenary birth celebrations of Bhagwan Swaminarayan in 1981 that Pramukh Swami visit her home. This was fulfilled by Swamishri exactly three years later.

stories.line: “How should we prepare for your visit?” | Mahant Swami Maharaj in London 2023
stories.story: “How should we prepare for your visit?” | Mahant Swami Maharaj in London 2023 A few weeks prior to his arrival in London in 2023, Mahant Swami Maharaj was asked how devotees can best prepare for his visit to the UK. He guided everyone towards internal improvement – specifically, on increasing divyabhav (seeing the divinity in everyone) and personal purity through antardrashti (introspection).

Devotees from Luton, Milton Keynes and nearby centres had gathered in the early hours of the morning to be the first to welcome Mahant Swami Maharaj to the UK
Devotees of all ages warmly greeted Mahant Swami Maharaj as he departed from the airport

BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Neasden, London – popularly called ‘London Mandir’ and ‘Neasden Temple’ Mahant Swami Maharaj had described London Mandir as “Our Home” during the Mandir’s 25th anniversary in 2020; a large sign bearing his handwritten message was ready to welcome him
Thousands of devotees and hundreds of volunteers had started arriving at London Mandir from as early as 3.30am in eager anticipation of Swamishri's arrival
As the van turned into Pramukh Swami Road, volunteers offered their dandvats to Thakorji and Swamishri

Children and devotees of all ages eagerly greeted Swamishri as he entered the Mandir
Children were equally excited and pleased to see Swamishri in London, some for the very first time
Devotees young and old cheered, waved flags and folded hands as Swamishri came closer
As Swamishri was about to enter the assembly hall, the jubilation among devotees steadily heightened

Swamishri’s path throughout the Mandir had been flanked by various origami (artistically folded paper) shapes symbolising various aspects of ‘The Divyabhav Project’ and ‘The Antardrashti Project’ that he had advised would be the best way to prepare for his visitTo learn more about this unique devotional welcome, please click here

The Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan, visited London Mandir (popularly known as ‘Neasden Temple’) on Sunday 21 May 2023 to meet His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj

In a personal meeting with Mahant Swami Maharaj, the Mayor said, “I am here as the leader of London to pay my respects to you and also to thank you because this community does so much good for Hindus and non-Hindus.”
The Mayor enjoyed the cultural programme being presented in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj
The Mayor sought the blessings of Mahant Swami Maharaj

In directly addressing Mahant Swami Maharaj, Mr Khan said, “We’ve had an awful two or three years because of the [Covid-19] pandemic, but during those dark times, you and your community were the light.”
The Mayor of London was honoured in the assembly by Anandswarupdas Swami on behalf of Mahant Swami Maharaj
Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed the Mayor of London, Sadiq Khan

stories.line: Yogiji Maharaj arrives in the UK from Kampala to open the Islington mandir
stories.story: For the opening of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Islington, London, Yogiji Maharaj graced the land of UK from 23 May to 7 July 1970 for 46 days and left lasting memories for countless haribhaktas and built the foundation for the development of satsang in UK-Europe.

stories.line: For the opening of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Islington
stories.story: For the opening of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Islington, London, Yogiji Maharaj graced the land of UK from 23 May to 7 July 1970 for 46 days and left lasting memories for countless haribhaktas and built the foundation for the development of satsang in UK-Europe. 23 May 1970 was also the first time that Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Mahant Swami Maharaj were stepping foot in the west. Click on the below link for smruti of this historic day through archive videos, eyewitness interviews, audios of telephone conversations, and the unique recording from the 'palen'.

stories.line: Yogiji Maharaj cuts a cake at his final Yogi Jayanti in Islington
stories.story: As part of a series of Yogi Jayanti celebrations at different locations across London in 1970, the fifth and final Yogi Jayanti was celebrated in Islington, London. Yogiji Maharaj is offered a cake by Prafulbhai on this occasion and grants divine bliss by cutting the cake and blowing the candles.

stories.line: Yogiji Maharaj signs a photo of Pramukh Swami, writing this is my swarup
stories.story: Yogiji Maharaj reveals Pramukh Swami Maharaj's mahima with the words, "Ā amāru swarup chhe." On 3 June 1970, Yogeshwar Swami brought a photograph of Pramukh Swami performing puja to show to Yogiji Maharaj. Yogiji Maharaj had a red pen in his hand. Immediately he signed the photo, ‘London, Date 3-6-70, Sadhu Jnanjivandasji’.

stories.line: As part of a series of Yogi Jayanti celebrations at different locations across London in 1970
stories.story: As part of a series of Yogi Jayanti celebrations at different locations across London in 1970, the fifth and final Yogi Jayanti was celebrated in Islington, London. Yogiji Maharaj is offered a cake by Prafulbhai on this occasion and grants divine bliss by cutting the cake and blowing the candles. A unique smruti can be observed whereby Pramukh Swami prompts Yogiji Maharaj to blow the remaining candles.

stories.line: Yogiji Maharaj blesses devotees and an afternoon sabha in Leicester
stories.story: After 14 days in London, Yogiji Maharaj departed from London on 6 June to give labh to the upcountry haribhaktas despite his advanced age and fragile health. On Sunday 7 June, Yogiji Maharaj blessed devotees at the residence of Bhupendrabhai Bhatt and graced the afternoon sabha held at Wesley Hall in Leicester.

stories.line: After 14 days in London
stories.story: After 14 days in London, Yogiji Maharaj departed from London on 6 June to give labh to the upcountry haribhaktas despite his advanced age and fragile health. On Sunday 7 June, Yogiji Maharaj blessed devotees at the residence of Bhupendrabhai Bhatt and graced the afternoon sabha held at Wesley Hall in Leicester. Pramukh Swami also conducted over 20 padharamanis on that day in Leicester.

In these three days, Swamishri graced all delegates with divine, unforgettable, joyful memories through unique interactions and ashirwads.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj graces the national family shibir in Nottingham
stories.story: On this day in 2000, Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced the National Family Shibir and Bal Balika Mandal Shibir at the University of Nottingham.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj blesses the National Family Shibir in Nottingham

stories.line: Yogiji Maharaj bathes Thakorji in the River Thames
stories.story: After departing from Dollis Hill at 10.30am, Yogiji Maharaj reached the area close to Putney Boating Club. Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami suggested that Thakorji be bathed with normal water after which the sanctified water could then be added to the Thames. But Yogiji Maharaj insisted on bathing Thakorji in the river itself.

stories.line: On Saturday 16 July 1977
stories.story: On Saturday 16 July 1977, almost six years after the Satsang Mandal in Manchester had begun with a handful of devotees, His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj opened a small mandir in Ashton-under-Lyne. The murtis that Yogiji Maharaj had originally installed in Islington in 1970 were re-installed at a small premises in Cowhill Lane following the yagna ceremony at the Indian Association Hall. [The murtis were subsequently moved to larger premises after the property in Russell Street was acquired in 1980.]

stories.line: Thousands flocked to Queens Park Rangers football stadium
stories.story: Thousands flocked to Queens Park Rangers football stadium, Loftus Road, West London, on the afternoon of 20 July 1985. Everyone was eager to witness the ‘Suvarna Mahotsav’, where Swamishri would be weighed against sugar crystals. Having been gifted with the greatest honour one can offer a spiritual master, Swamishri rose to bless the Suvarna Mahotsav congregation with great humility and love, as he revealed, “Firstly, I would like to offer my humble prostrations to the supreme Bhagwan Swaminarayan for this body he has blessed me with, and to Guru Shastriji Maharaj and Guru Yogiji Maharaj, who have blessed me and accepted me as theirs.

stories.line: Satsang had been established in Leicester following Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970
stories.story: Satsang had been established in Leicester following Yogiji Maharaj’s visit in 1970, and further consolidated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s vicharan in 1974. The local devotees were inspired by Swamishri to search for a place to worship. On the morning of Sunday 24 July 1977, Swamishri joined 70 devotees in the yagna ceremony, before consecrating the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj at the new mandir in Leicester on 148 Doncaster Road, the third Akshar-Purushottam mandir in the UK.

stories.line: On Saturday 30 July (Adhik Shravan sud Punam)
stories.story: On Saturday 30 July (Adhik Shravan sud Punam), Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated a new mandir in Wellingborough, the third BAPS Swaminarayan mandir to be consecrated in a short span of 15 days. The pictorial murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Radha-Krishna Bhagwan and the Guru Parampara were part of a grand procession through the streets of Wellingborough. Hundreds of devotees gathered to make history as the first Hindu mandir in Wellingborough was opened at humble premises on Mill Road.

stories.line: Devotees hold a colourful nagar yatra in London for the Mandir Mahotsav
stories.story: A colourful and devotional nagar yatra took place on this day in the heart of the city of London. It was the first day of the six-day Mandir Mahotsav to mark the opening of Europe's largest traditional Hindu mandir, BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, in Neasden, London.

stories.line: Commencement of six-day Mandir Mahotsav celebrations to mark the opening of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
stories.story: Commencement of six-day Mandir Mahotsav celebrations to mark the opening of BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Neasden, London. Haveli keys formally handed over to Thakorji and Swamishri by Laxmanbhai (contractor) and Nigel Lane (chief architect). Nagar Yatra procession through Central London.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates London Mandir in Neasden
stories.story: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates London Mandir, the first traditional Hindu temple in the west. It had been 25 years since Yogiji Maharaj had declared his divine wish for a traditional mandir in London, spoken at the time of the opening of the small mandir in Islington in June 1970.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London
stories.story: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London, the first traditional Hindu temple in the west. It had been 25 years since Yogiji Maharaj had declared his divine wish for a traditional mandir in London, spoken at the time of the opening of the small mandir in Islington in June 1970.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurates the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London
stories.story: On this day in 1995, Pramukh Swami Maharaj inaugurated BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in London, the first traditional Hindu mandir in the west, fulfilling Yogiji Maharaj's wish.

stories.line: Mahant Swami Maharaj presides over a chhavani on Akshar Purushottam Darshan
stories.story: An all-day ‘chhavani’ (spiritual camp of discourses) on the fundamental principles of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan (upasana) was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj and senior swamis at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London.

stories.line: An all-day ‘chhavani’ (spiritual camp of discourses) on the fundamental principles of Akshar-Purushottam
stories.story: An all-day ‘chhavani’ (spiritual camp of discourses) on the fundamental principles of Akshar-Purushottam Darshan (upasana) was held in the presence of Mahant Swami Maharaj and senior swamis at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Mahant Swami Maharaj had expressed his wish for this special programme to be organised and personally encouraged everyone to attend. He drew upon the four-month chhavani that had been held in Vartal, India, during the time of Gunatitanand Swami and gave his blessings for a similar day of spiritual enrichment in London.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj makes an unexpected trip from Mumbai to London
stories.story: At 1.50pm, Swamishri departed by plane from Mumbai towards London. The flight landed at Heathrow at 6.50pm (GMT) and 11.20pm (IST). When Swamishri retired for the night, it was 10.00pm (GMT) and 2.30am (IST). See video highlights of the swagat and amazing ashirwad given on this very day.

stories.line: Pramukh Swami Maharaj flies to London for an unexpected month long stay
stories.story: An unexpected trip when Pramukh Swami Maharaj graced the UK, staying in London for one month. At 1.50pm, Swamishri departed by plane from Mumbai for London. The flight landed at London Heathrow Airport at 6.50pm GMT (11.20pm IST). When Swamishri retired for the night, it was 10.00pm GMT (2.30am IST).

stories.line: After learning in one of the recent discourses of the Shakotsav celebrated 170 years previously in Loya
stories.story: After learning in one of the recent discourses of the Shakotsav celebrated 170 years previously in Loya by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the devotees of London made a sankalp that such a shakotsav be celebrated in London as well. After due preparations were made, Param Pujya Swamishri went to the Mandir kitchen area around 4.50pm and personally conducted the shak vaghar in three big utensils in which a total of 10 maunds (200kg) of aubergines were prepared. After offering the final product to Harikrishna Maharaj, the devotees partook of this as prasad following the evening sabha.
